reason: Design as written does NOT discriminate: (1) no null arm (no random-residue LLL control, no unfiltered pair control, no planted-positive arm); (2) hit-count statistic is vacuous: p=2^24..2^32, alpha 1/16..1/8 gives B=p^alpha~4..16, |L1|~B^2/2<=128, pairs<=8e3, hit prob p^(alpha-1)~2^-28 => expected hits ~1e-5 per run; 'within 10%' is meaningless at 0 hits; B<=2^8 with alpha>=1/4 puts it outside stated alpha range; JM threshold 1/80 is asymptotic and p^(1/80)<2 at toy p so 'alpha>1/80' is vacuous; (3) conceptual flaw: S_3 numerators are small only for level-1 inputs in the interval. Level-2 inputs U=P1+P2, V=P3+P4 have full-size x mod p, so S_3 symmetric functions of (U,V) have no archimedean smallness; the filter has nothing to bite on at level 2. (4) Curve coefficients a,b are ~p: e1 numerator = 2(x1+x2)(x1x2+a)+4b ~ p^(1+alpha), not p^(3alpha), so even level-1 reconstruction is non-small on generic curves. I MEASURED this (python, 300 samples/cell, Euclid rational reconstruction, median log_p(N*D)): random a,b: 0.80/0.82/0.83 at p=2^24/28/32 (alpha=1/8) vs random-residue control 0.79/0.82/0.84, i.e. indistinguishable from null; small a,b (|a|,|b|<5): 0.31/0.33/0.36 at alpha=1/8 (~6alpha=0.75 bound loose) but 0.78-0.82 (= null) at alpha=1/4 since 6alpha>1. So the filter is only live for special small-coefficient curves and alpha<1/6; prediction_if_true is already falsified for random-a,b curves by a level-1-only run (<1 CPU-s). Runnable under 20 CPU-min in python3 yes (no PARI needed), but scaling to n=131: only the exponent statement scales (log_p(N*D) vs alpha at fixed curve class), hit-rate toy counts do not. Metric must be structural (reconstruction-size exponent, false-positive rate, enrichment), not wall time. Also even if filter worked it costs O(|L1|^2) LLL tests = same as sort-and-match, so BL-equal-advice audit/B*D^2<<N certificate not beaten by constant: expected class accounting/relabelling of lattice-reach wall (concur).
fix: Replace hit-count experiment by 3-arm size-exponent experiment. Arm A (signal): x1,x2 uniform in [1,p^alpha], e1=x(P+Q)+x(P-Q) and e2=x(P+Q)x(P-Q) from closed-form S_3 (Cassels formulas) mod p; Gauss/LLL 2x2 reconstruction of e1,e2 jointly; record s=log_p(min |N|*|D|). Arm B (null): uniform random residues mod p, same reconstruction. Arm C (control): same x1,x2 but curve family varied: random a,b ~p vs small |a|,|b|<=5 vs a,b of size p^alpha. Grid p in {2^24,2^28,2^32,2^40,2^48} (python bigints fine), alpha in {1/16,1/12,1/8,1/6,1/4}, >=2000 samples/cell, report median s, 5th percentile, and false-positive rate P_B(s<=s_threshold) with threshold chosen at 6alpha+0.05. Success metric = slope of s vs alpha and gap(A,B) at fixed alpha, tested across p (scaling-in-p is the n=131 transfer: exponent only). Then level-2 arm: take U=P1+P2,V=P3+P4 (use scalar/dlog representation: base points via lift_x with dlogs from PARI elllog at p<=2^32, sums as integers mod r, so no EC ops and no hit-starvation) and run the SAME reconstruction on S_3(x(U),x(V)); prediction: s equals null B within noise (no smallness at level 2). Planted-positive arm: choose 4-tuples with U+V in base (find by sorted dlog match, expect B^5/p hits, use p=2^20,B=2^8 to get ~2^20 hits) and test whether passing-filter set enriches hits: report enrichment = P(hit|pass)/P(hit) and pass-rate, with enrichment 1.0 as null. Count ops (LLL calls, pairs examined) vs generic sort-match n^4K^4/r baseline. Decision rule: true only if A-B gap in s persists on random-a,b curves AND level-2 enrichment >1 growing in p; expected outcome: gap vanishes for random a,b, level-2 enrichment=1 -> classify accounting/relabelling.
